title: Slide a tray of soup out of a serving pass with both hands, set it on the table, then serve the bowl
instruction: With both hands on the tray's side rims, slide the tray out of the pass and set it down flat on the table without spilling the soup, then put the bowl on the blue placemat.
context: Food runners take loaded trays off a kitchen pass, often from under a shelf, set them down and serve from them: the soup cannot be reached until the tray is drawn out, and tipping the tray on the way down spills it.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed wooden serving pass on the centre line: a lower shelf, a block 12 cm deep (front to back), 24 cm wide and 12 cm tall with its front edge 25 cm forward; and an upper shelf 1 cm thick and 20 cm wide, from 27.5 to 41 cm forward, its underside 21 cm above the table, held up by a back panel at 40 to 41 cm. (2) A dark grey plastic serving tray, 36 cm wide (side to side) and 20 cm deep, with a 6 mm floor and rims 1.6 cm tall and 5 mm thick, 0.35 kg, loose, resting on the lower shelf centred 30 cm forward on the centre line; its left and right rims stick out past the pass. (3) A white ceramic soup bowl, inside 9 cm across and 5 cm deep, with a flat handle 3.5 cm long, 2 cm tall and 8 mm thick sticking out to the right, 0.25 kg, standing in the middle of the tray under the upper shelf. (4) The soup: 15 orange plastic beads 8 mm across, 1.5 g each, in the bowl. (5) A round blue placemat 13 cm across, flat on the table, its centre 32 cm forward and 26 cm right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial, placing each bead by its centre. 0.0 if the bowl is ever tipped 45 degrees or more, or ends tilted 15 degrees or more. Otherwise 1.0 with the bowl standing on the placemat (its centre within 4 cm of the placemat's centre), the tray lying flat on the table (tilted less than 10 degrees) and at most 1 of the 15 beads out of the bowl; 0.5 with the tray lying flat on the table and at most 3 beads out of the bowl, but the bowl not on the placemat; 0.25 with the tray drawn wholly out in front of the lower shelf (but not lying on the table) and at most 3 beads out of the bowl; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with everything still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: put the beads back in the bowl, stand the bowl in the middle of the tray with its handle to the right, and slide the tray back onto the lower shelf, centred.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the soup is 15 rigid 8 mm beads standing in for liquid (they roll and spill but do not slosh); the bowl's round wall is 20 flat panels; the pass is three plain blocks; friction is set (tray 0.5, bowl 0.6, beads 0.3); the cameras render at 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
